chunks: He عليه السلام was asked about a man who became angry and said: “Upon me is to walk to the Sacred House of Allah.”
He عليه السلام said: “If he did not say, ‘For Allah upon me,’ then it is nothing.”

key_terms.الْمَشْيُ: walking; the act the speaker intended to obligate upon himself
key_terms.بَيْتِ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامِ: the Sacred House of Allah; the Ka'bah in Makkah
key_terms.بِشَيْءٍ: anything of consequence; here meaning legally ineffective or non-binding
key_terms.عَلَيَّ: upon me; wording that suggests self-imposition of an act
key_terms.غَضِبَ: became angry; indicates the statement was made in a state of anger
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: for Allah; the wording that establishes the statement as a vow to Allah

ai.seo_question: Does saying in anger, “Upon me is to walk to the House of Allah,” count as a binding vow?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a statement uttered in anger concerning walking to the Sacred House of Allah. It indicates that such words do not constitute a binding nadhr unless they are explicitly formulated as an obligation to Allah.
